scope.summary: Implement the shipped Tailor product-contract semantic gate used by CI and qualification to cross-check the runtime capability, action, operation, surface, UserManual, diagnostics, profile, and artifact registries; the existing preactivation MT checker remains governance prep outside this MT.
acceptance_criteria: The gate rejects missing or duplicate capability/action/operation/surface/manual/profile identifiers, any missing exact TAI-ACT-010 Tailor seed action, unresolved TAI-ACT-008..009 schema or event owners, action/manual drift, unsupported authority paths, diagnostic-posture contradictions, product-fixture misplacement, and unqualified required capabilities.

It validates native and backend route parity, actor/session/correlation/version/idempotency/lease fields, preview-diff-apply and recovery semantics, exact surface/help anchors, and ArtifactStore/EventLedger/Flight Recorder lineage without reading governance MT files at runtime.

CI emits a deterministic machine-readable report artifact and nonzero failure status; runtime diagnostics may project the last report but the report never changes capability qualification or validator verdict by itself.
scope.risk_if_missed: A large MT inventory can hide omissions and contradictory obligations unless every contract is mechanically reviewed through the required lenses.

gui_obligation.not_applicable_reason: Non-UI contract: typed commands, state, receipts, diagnostics, and TraceProjection provide model/operator observability; the owning native projection is separately contracted.

target_entries: Tailor UserManual > Run and repair the Tailor product-contract semantic gate

hbr_int_009_tier_obligations.reason: This MT implements a deterministic CI/product-contract check and does not own an authority or job lifecycle; it verifies Flight Recorder bindings declared by the checked runtime contracts.
The gate emits a report and test failure rather than a runtime diagnostic operation; it validates internal_diagnostics coverage on the product contracts it inspects.
The CI check is bounded and owns no watched native or external process; it verifies Palmistry classification for long-running Tailor operations.

risks: A large MT inventory can hide omissions and contradictory obligations unless every contract is mechanically reviewed through the required lenses.
GUI, backend, agent, replay, and manual projections may drift if they do not consume the same typed authority.
minimum_controls: One typed owner and exact stable ids are required.
Negative, concurrent, cancellation, recovery, and no-context proofs are required where applicable.
No validator PASS/FAIL is inferred from this pre-activation contract.
